items.title: Steep bill for AI buildout punishes Meta, other tech favorites
items.author: Lewis Krauskopf, Sudeshna Ghoshal
items.creator: Lewis Krauskopf, Sudeshna Ghoshal
items.summary: The tab for the next round of the AI buildout came due on Thursday.
items.body:
The tab for the next round of the AI buildout came due on Thursday.
Investors sold shares of Meta Platforms (META.O) and a wealth of companies central to the AI trade, a day after Meta -- one of the so-called hyperscalers spending billions to build data centers and other infrastructure supporting the AI boom -- said it would issue a new class of shares that will help it raise funds.
Meta fell 8%, its largest drop since July. SpaceX (SPCX.O) declined 9% and semiconductor giant Nvidia (NVDA.O) -- a bellwether of the AI trade -- dropped 4%. The Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) was on track for its largest decline in four months.
A 10% plunge in shares of semiconductor company Lam Research (LRCX.O) following its results also weighed on sentiment and sent the semiconductor index (.SOX) to its largest decline since July.
The pullback is the latest test for the AI trade, focusing on the rising costs of a long-term project the payoffs from which remain uncertain and will likely be unevenly distributed. Tech firms have borrowed huge sums over the past year for AI spending, but Wall Street now expects that higher interest rates mean the likes of Meta will sell billions of dollars in stock to fund the next round of building – putting pressure on share prices by increasing the number of shares outstanding.
It is an unwelcome development in a market where major US stock indexes remain near all-time highs despite a punishing month of volatile trading.
Selling started with "the big question about the (return on investment) on all the spending," said Matthew Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak. "It's just becoming more and more evident to people that it's going to take a lot longer."
Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital LLC in New York, agreed that ROI concerns are central while also citing reported remarks by Nvidia (NVDA.O) CEO Jensen Huang about a financing bottleneck for smaller AI companies as contributing to the selling.
Meta on Wednesday said it would use new Class C shares, which hold no voting power, to fund AI spending and other priorities . Meta also raised the low end of its annual spending forecast to $135 billion from $130 billion, with the high end unchanged at $145 billion.
That level of spending will require lots of investor participation in coming stock sales. Meta reported negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, compared with positive free cash flow of $10.63 billion a year earlier. It was the first cash burn at Meta in more than a decade.
“More spending, negative free cash flow, not enough revenue being generated from the spend (is) concerning investors that this is just sort of a bit of a money pit,” said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield, Connecticut.
The action highlights concern over how AI investment will be paid for. Credit default swaps tracking perceived default risk of many of the biggest AI players have risen over the past year, with Meta’s hitting a record on Thursday – reflecting uncertainty over who will benefit most from the sums being spent now.
Fresh signs of market pressure to curb spending on AI quickly translated on Thursday into a broad market selloff reflecting expectations that any AI pullback would hit US growth, resulting in a sharp rally in Treasury prices .
“The market seems to be real-time repricing the probabilities of a US ‘growth scare’ off the back of the AI reset,” Nomura Securities strategist Charlie McElligott wrote in a note to clients.
Thursday’s selloff added to the pressure on the so-called neocloud companies at the heart of the AI buildout, with Nebius (NBIS.O) off 7% after announcing a new $3.5 billion credit line from Citigroup and CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , whose unsecured bond yields soared to 15% in last week’s AI selloff, down 9%.
Bank of America analyst Tal Liani said in a report on Thursday he maintains a buy rating and a price target of $140 on CoreWeave stock heading into next month’s earnings report, though he said he believes the firm will need to raise $20 billion to fund commitments to customers -- the sort of prospect that is generating investor anxiety now across the technology industry.
"Nobody is worried about Meta or Amazon or Google getting the financing they need," Maley said. "But if it gets prohibitive for smaller companies, then you don't have to have an implosion of things to make people nervous."

items.title: Merck/Moderna cancer vaccine cuts risk of melanoma death or recurrence by over 40%
items.author: Julie Steenhuysen, Michael Erman
items.creator: Julie Steenhuysen, Michael Erman
items.summary: Moderna and Merck said on Thursday that the mRNA cancer vaccine they developed combined with a widely used immunotherapy cut the risk of death or recurrence of melanoma by 42% and disease spread by 38% in a large trial.
items.body:
Moderna (MRNA.O) and Merck (MRK.N) said on Thursday that the mRNA cancer vaccine they developed combined with a widely used immunotherapy cut the risk of death or recurrence of melanoma by 42% and disease spread by 38% in a large trial.
The data from the Phase 3 trial of more than 1,100 patients potentially paves the way for a new era of personalized treatment. Moderna and Merck [USN:L1N44F0SC TEXT:"announced in August"] that the treatment had succeeded but did not provide details from the trial.
It is the first to show that the combination of a vaccine based on mutations unique to each patient's tumor plus a drug that helps the immune system fight cancer can keep the disease at bay. The vaccine was tested along with Merck's blockbuster immunotherapy Keytruda, among the world's biggest-selling medicines.
Moderna shares, which have rocketed since the August trial announcement, nearly quadrupling through Wednesday's close, fell over 20% after the results leaked on an oncology website earlier on Thursday. Merck shares were down about 0.7%.
The results, based on patient data for the first two years after treatment, are scheduled to be presented on Saturday at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid.
Several Wall Street analysts said before the meeting that investors were looking for the combination to cut the risk of recurrence by 40% or more.
"This is highly statistically significant. It is not by chance," Dr. Hussein Tawbi, a melanoma expert and trial investigator at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, said of the results.
The trial tested nine doses of the vaccine, known as intismeran, along with Keytruda, beginning 13 weeks after surgery to remove melanoma lesions. Their response was compared with patients treated with just Keytruda, a standard therapy for melanoma.
Among those who received the vaccine in addition to Keytruda, 82.2% were still cancer-free after two years, compared with 70% of patients who received Keytruda alone.

Oct 22 : Police are investigating a break-in at Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes' house in which intruders stole a number of items, according to a report by The Athletic.
Cheshire Police launched an investigation after officers responded to reports of suspicious activity on Wednesday night at a residential address.
"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property," Detective Inspector Dave Jarvis told The Athletic.
"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."
The report said that police were alerted shortly after Manchester United's 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como in Italy.
According to The Athletic, citing a club statement, no members of Fernandes' family were at the property during the break-in and the intruders spent less than five minutes inside before police arrived.
Reuters has contacted Cheshire Police and Manchester United for comment.
Fernandes has featured in every game for United this season and captained the side on Wednesday as they extended their winless run in all competitions to seven matches.
Following the defeat, the 32-year-old called on his team to be "more brave" after another disappointing result.
United, who are 13th in the Premier League standings, host Bournemouth on Sunday.

items.title: Inundaciones provocadas por El Niño desplazan a miles en Paraguay mientras lluvias azotan Sudamérica
items.author: Cesar Olmedo
items.creator: Cesar Olmedo
items.summary: En el predio de la parroquia San Agustín, situada en uno de los barrios más afectados por las inundaciones causadas por el fenómeno climático El Niño en Paraguay, más de 30 familias se refugian de las lluvias y comparten alimentos donados mientras sus casas permanecen bajo agua.
items.body:
En el predio de la parroquia San Agustín, situada en uno de los barrios más afectados por las inundaciones causadas por el fenómeno climático El Niño en Paraguay, más de 30 familias se refugian de las lluvias y comparten alimentos donados mientras sus casas permanecen bajo agua.
Ubicados en Ciudad del Este, en la frontera con Brasil, San Agustín y San Rafael son dos de los barrios con mayor número de damnificados en el país por la crecida del caudaloso río Paraná y sus afluentes, en medio de las intensas precipitaciones atribuidas al evento meteorológico que han golpeado también a regiones de Chile, Argentina, Brasil y Perú.
"Tuvimos que salir todos de nuestras casas porque (....) ya en varias oportunidades el agua ha tomado parte de nuestros hogares", dijo a Reuters Vicente Montiel, en el predio de la parroquia, donde varias familias se instalaron en carpas en una cancha de fútbol y organizan ollas comunes con la ayuda de la iglesia y empresas locales que proveen víveres.
"No sabemos todavía si el agua va a retornar porque esta vez muchas familias quedaron con sus techos bajo agua y a pesar de que (el río) bajó, dicen que va a volver de nuevo. Vamos a estar acá hasta que se regularice el clima y el agua pare".
La crecida del río Paraná ha dejado unas 4.200 familias damnificadas en Paraguay, en los departamentos del sureste del territorio que bordean el cauce, según la Secretaría de Emergencia Nacional (SEN). Una mujer de 58 años de Ciudad del Este murió la semana pasada tras el derrumbe de su vivienda debido a los fuertes raudales.
MÁS LLUVIAS Ante el último pronóstico del miércoles de tormentas severas, las autoridades pidieron a los damnificados que no vuelvan a sus hogares y está trabajando para identificar más lugares donde construir viviendas temporales para albergues.
La mayoría de las casas de los barrios San Rafael y San Agustín siguen bajo el agua y sus pobladores recorren las calles en pequeños botes para rescatar objetos que puedan salvarse o vigilar la zona.
"Me sorprendió porque llegó muy rápido (el agua). Mi casa, mi cocina se cayó toda, se está derrumbando", dijo Antonina Sánchez, de 65 años, en San Rafael. "El barrio está todo tomado (...) muchas cosas perdimos y necesitamos mucho".
El nivel del río en esa zona descendió levemente luego de alcanzar un máximo el 15 de octubre, pero las autoridades temen que vuelva a repuntar con las próximas lluvias previstas. El titular de la SEN, Arsenio Zárate, estimó que hasta 15.000 viviendas podrían sufrir las consecuencias de una nueva subida del río.
"Estamos recabando los datos para ir reponiendo las mercaderías, ir completando lo que va faltando en cada toldo, en cada carpa", dijo a Reuters el director de Desarrollo Social de la alcaldía de Ciudad del Este, Julio Landaia. "Las ollas populares están continuamente siendo abastecidas".
Funcionarios de la ONU advirtieron esta semana que el actual episodio de El Niño podría ser de una intensidad sin precedentes. Se espera que las temperaturas en el Pacífico central superen el promedio en unos 3,8 grados Celsius entre noviembre y enero, alcanzando su punto máximo alrededor de diciembre.
El Niño se está haciendo sentir también en otras partes de América Latina. En Argentina, dos trabajadores rurales fallecieron mientras trasladaban ganado fuera de zonas inundadas próximas al río Paraná en la provincia de Corrientes, donde cientos de residentes han sido evacuados.
En Perú, las autoridades anunciaron el jueves medidas de ayuda financiera y alivio fiscal para las empresas afectadas por fenómenos meteorológicos extremos frente a la costa del Pacífico.
Parte de un complejo de condominios de lujo en la costa del Pacífico mexicano colapsó el miércoles, después de que el fuerte oleaje erosionara la arena bajo la edificación, dejando al descubierto sus cimientos y provocando que la estructura quedara peligrosamente inclinada hacia el mar.

items.title: Ex-prosecutor’s killing puts Guatemala’s crime-politics nexus back in focus
items.author: The Straits Times
items.summary: GUATEMALA CITY, Oct 22 - Former Guatemalan anti-corruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa was one of the country's most high profile voices denouncing alleged links between politicians and business leaders and the country's increasingly powerful organized crime groups.
items.body:
Ex-prosecutor’s killing puts Guatemala’s crime-politics nexus back in focus
Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

Published   Oct 23, 2026, 02:16 AM

Updated   Oct 23, 2026, 02:16 AM

Set as preferred source

GUATEMALA CITY, Oct 22 - Former Guatemalan anti-corruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa was one of the country's most high profile voices denouncing alleged links between politicians and business leaders and the country's increasingly powerful organized crime groups.
Over the weekend, he was shot dead on a soccer field, a killing that former officials and diplomats consulted by Reuters said has heightened concerns over organized crime's influence in the Central American nation.
The killing of an outspoken former prosecutor who had publicly challenged powerful interests shocked the country and revived debate over criminal networks’ penetration of state institutions.

"This is a threat against human rights defenders. This is a threat against activists for democracy," said Frank La Rue, a human rights advocate, who attended the wake for Solorzano Foppa on Monday, which featured portraits of the slain lawyer with his family.
For many Guatemalans, it recalled the 1998 assassination of Bishop Juan Jose Gerardi, beaten to death two days after presenting a report documenting atrocities from the country’s civil war, and stirred fears that violence could again be used against prominent critics of powerful interests.
Experts said criminal networks have strengthened their influence in recent years as anti-corruption efforts and institutions tasked with combating impunity have weakened, issues likely to loom over the June 2027 election as Guatemala chooses President Bernardo Arevalo’s successor.

Authorities have not established a motive for Solorzano Foppa's killing. But officials and diplomats said the case has fueled concerns about criminal groups’ ability to intimidate or silence critical voices.
More than 100 former prosecutors, judges, journalists and human rights defenders have left Guatemala in recent years, according to some international human rights organizations, after denouncing corruption or alleged links between state structures and criminal networks.
This week, following Solorzano Foppa's killing, a high-profile lawyer who also railed against political corruption said he has received death threats. On Wednesday, Arevalo denounced the threats against the lawyer, Edgar Ortiz.

"Guatemala cannot return to being a country where defending democracy can cost one peace, freedom, or their life," Arevalo wrote on social media.
'RED LINE CROSSED'
Corruption has been a major institutional challenge in Guatemala for decades. From 2007 to 2019, the UN-backed International Commission against Impunity in Guatemala (CICIG) helped investigate corruption and organized crime networks within the state, including cases that led to the resignation and subsequent prosecution of then-President Otto Perez Molina and his former vice president, Roxana Baldetti.
Since CICIG's departure in 2019, human rights groups, prosecutors and international observers have denounced setbacks in the fight against corruption. President Arevalo, who took office in 2024 promising to tackle the problem, has acknowledged difficulties advancing reforms and dismantling structures accused of corruption.
In videos posted on Facebook, TikTok and Instagram, and seen by Reuters, Solorzano Foppa alleged links between Barrio 18 leader Aldo "El Lobo" Ochoa, who is serving combined prison sentences of more than 1,600 years, and people close to the leadership of the National Unity of Hope (UNE) party, headed by former first lady Sandra Torres. Reuters could not independently verify the allegations.
UNE told Reuters in a statement that "those allegations were never proven and should not be presented as established facts."
Solorzano Foppa, a former head of Guatemala's SAT tax administration agency, also alleged ties between criminal networks, political figures and sectors of the judicial system, though the accusations did not result in judicial proceedings.
Officials have not identified who ordered the killing. The Organization of American States and the United Nations have called for a thorough investigation.
The Public Prosecutor's Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. On Sunday, following the murder, it said in a statement that "in order to guarantee due process, it will not disclose additional details about the evidence gathered or the specific lines of investigation."
A former government official, who was not authorized to speak publicly, said insiders had turned to Solorzano Foppa with information they felt unable to expose themselves, making him an outlet for allegations from within the state. His killers "left no trace," the former official said, complicating the investigation.
Guatemala's criminal networks range from gangs and drug traffickers to structures involving former officials and members of the security forces. Analysts say some have retained influence over state institutions, while armed groups like Barrio 18 and Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13) remain involved in extortion and territorial control.
They include the so-called CIACS, or Illegal Clandestine Security Apparatuses, networks linked to former security structures that experts say retain political and economic influence. Guatemala is also a major drug-trafficking corridor to the United States, with groups associated with Mexico's Sinaloa Cartel and Jalisco New Generation Cartel operating through local criminal networks.
"Many of us fear that a red line has been crossed," said Stephen McFarland, former US ambassador to Guatemala from 2008 to 2011. "A return to political assassination as a way of settling scores and protecting the ambitions and money of certain people." REUTERS

items.title: Chiefs placing LT Josh Simmons (back) on injured reserve
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Kansas City Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons' rehab from a back injury has "plateaued" and he will be placed on injured reserve.
items.body:
Kansas City Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons' rehab from a back injury has "plateaued" and he will be placed on injured reserve.
Head trainer Rick Burkholder provided an update Thursday on Simmons, who has been dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back since training camp.
"Josh worked his tail off," Burkholder told reporters. "He worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week. ...
"However, we feel he's plateaued in the rehab process as he's trying to get to the final steps of recovery with a return to competition. And he's just not there yet."
Simmons, 23, has missed the first five games for the Chiefs (5-0) and now will have to miss at least four more on IR. He will not be eligible to return until the Week 11 game against the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 22.
"He'll continue with the rehab process with the goal of returning to play at a high level that he achieved in the past," Burkholder said. "I just give (Simmons) a ton of credit for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended and that he needs more time to return to full function."
A 2025 first-round draft pick, Simmons made eight starts as a rookie last season. He missed four games in midseason for a personal matter and then missed the last five games after going on IR following a wrist injury.
Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has started at left tackle in Simmons' absence.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Lamar Jackson hits practice field, Ravens like chances of return
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Lamar Jackson walked onto the practice field with teammates on Thursday with plans to participate as he works his way back from injuring his ankle on Oct. 4 against the Tennessee Titans.
items.body:
Lamar Jackson walked onto the practice field with teammates on Thursday with plans to participate as he works his way back from injuring his ankle on Oct. 4 against the Tennessee Titans.
The two-time MVP quarterback missed two games -- a Baltimore win at Atlanta and last week's loss in Cleveland -- recovering from the injury. He last played in the first half of the Ravens' Week 4 win over the Titans.
"Any time he's out there, it kind of elevates the whole group. We're certainly excited about the direction that he's heading," Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said Thursday. "He's still got a lot of work to do in order to be able to play on Sunday, but he's really working at it behind the scenes. It's great having him in the meeting room. And it's another thing to be able to have him out there on the field with us and continuing to push and his teammates seeing him push and all that stuff."
Jackson has six TD passes and one interception plus a rushing touchdown in 14 total quarters played in 2026. In his stead, Baltimore turned to Tyler Huntley at quarterback.
Even with a much-improved defense, the Bengals -- Sunday's opponent -- are not a team likely to be thrilled to see Jackson on the field. He's 11-2 as a starter against Cincinnati with 3,699 total yards (2,868 passing) and 26 TDs (two rushing TDs).
"Tyler's played a lot of games for them over the years, done a really good job," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. "I don't think anybody replaces Lamar, just one for one. But Tyler does a great job where I don't feel like they have to change anything that they're really doing. He can still make plays with his feet, he's made a lot of plays with his arm. He's smart, he understands their system. I think he's played really well for them over the years."
Both Baltimore quarterbacks planned to take reps with the first team on Thursday in preparation for Sunday's game.
The Ravens are one of three 4-2 teams in the AFC North and lead the division in points (156) while ranking last in points allowed (132). Baltimore has 116 points and 14 touchdowns with Jackson at quarterback this season, compared to 40 points and four touchdowns without him.
--Field Level Media

Analysts say some have retained influence over state institutions, while armed groups like Barrio 18 and Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13) remain involved in extortion and territorial control.
They include the so-called CIACS, or Illegal Clandestine Security Apparatuses, networks linked to former security structures that experts say retain political and economic influence. Guatemala is also a major drug-trafficking corridor to the United States, with groups associated with Mexico's Sinaloa Cartel and Jalisco New Generation Cartel operating through local criminal networks.
"Many of us fear that a red line has been crossed," said Stephen McFarland, former US ambassador to Guatemala from 2008 to 2011. "A return to political assassination as a way of settling scores and protecting the ambitions and money of certain people."

items.title: Silver inflows likely to rebound as import curbs eased for Diwali
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Fresh import permits are set to ease India's silver supply constraints and premiums ahead of Diwali, though demand is expected to trail last year's levels ...
items.body: India’s silver imports are set to rebound in time for the busiest jewelry-buying season after the government issued a raft of new permits, easing restrictions that had stifled shipments to one of the world’s biggest markets. Traders and bank dealers this week received quotas covering as much as 6,000 tonnes of silver, said according to four people familiar with the matter. The permits are valid for six months, said the people, who asked not to be named because they’re not allowed to speak publicly. The new licences “should be able to easily cover any demand spike,” said Harshal Barot, principal consultant at Metals Focus Ltd, a precious metals consultancy. “As a result, we no longer see a tight market and premiums are likely to ease substantially in the run-up to Diwali.” India imports almost all of its silver. The government  introduced new licensing requirements in May, one of a number of measures taken to preserve foreign-exchange reserves and defend the rupee.  Would-be silver buyers must now apply for a permit, and every shipment must be accompanied by a certificate proving the country of origin. The government also more than doubled import taxes on gold and silver, adding to the cost of buying. As a result, silver imports initially plunged to a fraction of the country’s demand. In June, monthly shipments hit a three-year low of just 37 tonnes. That rose to 328 tonnes in September, according to an estimate by Metals Focus, as a limited num­ber of permits were granted.  Demand for precious metals typically rises during the festival season that peaks with Diwali. With the latest permits granted, premiums paid to secure silver are likely to ease substantially, Barot said. Indian premiums dropped to around 50 cents an ounce over the global benchmark on Thursday, said Monal Thakkar, managing director of Ashoka Global FZCO, a precious metals trader. That was down from around $2 last week, data from Metals Focus shows. Last year, India imported over 7,000 tonnes of silver, a massive wave of buying that helped to trigger a historic short squeeze in the global market. Prices rose further as speculators piled in — hitting a record high above $121 an ounce in January — before slumping after the West Asia war sent energy prices surging, stoking global inflation fears. Spot silver was trading around $56 an ounce on Thursday. While demand has picked up ahead of the festival season, silver consumption is expected to pale in comparison with last year. Stocking by retailers and wholesalers has been subdued, Barot said, and fewer Indians are gifting silver this year. “We have not seen any meaningful dip-buying despite the price correction, as many investors are sitting on losses from silver bought last year,” he added.  Restrictions lifted Traders, bank dealers have received quotas covering as much as 6,000 tonnes of silverThe Centre introduced licensing requirements in May as a measure to conserve Fx reservesAs a result, silver imports initially plunged to a fraction of the country’s demandDespite demand uptick, silver consumption is expected to pale in comparison with last year

items.title: Egypt calls for Yemen talks as parliament weighs military support to Saudi Arabia
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Egypt advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically, its foreign minister said, ahead of a parliamentary vote next week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis.
items.body:
Egypt advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically, its foreign minister said, ahead of a parliamentary vote next week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis.
Any direct involvement of the Egyptian military, one of the region's largest, would raise the stakes in the conflict between the kingdom and the Houthis, an increasingly destabilising front in the spreading US-Israeli war on Iran .
President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Saturday for an urgent parliamentary session to authorise military involvement supporting the kingdom. After a closed session on Sunday, lawmakers [USN:S8N44Y029 TEXT:"postponed the vote until October 26"] to allow more deliberation.
Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be [USN:S8N45S05P TEXT:"limited to defending Saudi territory"] and borders rather than attacking Yemen.
What kind of support Egypt will ultimately provide remains unclear.
EGYPT HAS LIMITED ROLE IN SAUDI-LED YEMEN COALITION Abdelatty said on Thursday that Egypt underlined the need to "explore every opportunity for the possibility of reaching political solutions" ensuring a full Houthi withdrawal from territory seized during the group's advance in September near [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"the Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] — a critical chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth and gateway to Egypt's Suez Canal.
"So that we can move on the political path that we always emphasize, and also side by side in support of the defensive path for the kingdom," Abdelatty told a press conference.
Clashes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognized government have intensified since the group's push towards Bab el-Mandeb on the Red Sea further strained global oil supplies. The militia has since [USN:S8N44908G TEXT:"attacked Saudi airports and oil facilities"].
Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, is a vital strategic and economic partner for Egypt, providing billions in aid, central bank deposits and energy supplies under Sisi.
The war in Yemen, which has caused a humanitarian crisis, started in 2014 when the Houthis drove the internationally recognised government out of the northern capital, drawing Saudi-led military intervention.
Egypt joined the Saudi-led coalition in March 2015 mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes while pledging air support. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but played only a limited combat role.
A US-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted attacks.
While Cairo has voiced support for Riyadh since the resumption of hostilities, it has avoided direct combat. It did not join the Mecca mutual defense pact linking Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, though it says membership remains under consideration.
The Saudi crown prince [USN:P8N3ZN0LL TEXT:"sought military assistance from the United States"], but President Donald Trump did not agree to the US striking Houthis, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters in September. Washington told Riyadh that it would help with intelligence sharing and targeting, they added.
Yahya Ali al-Rai, speaker of the Houthi-run House of Representatives, warned on Saturday against Egyptian involvement, urging parliament to reject the proposal. "Should Egypt slide down this path, it would pose a grave threat to its own national security and internal stability," he said.
items.raw_description: Egypt advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically, its foreign minister said, ahead of a parliamentary vote next week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

items.title: Caída a nivel nacional de Davivienda en Colombia hoy 22 de octubre: no funciona la app ni la web
items.author: Redacción Bloomberg Línea
items.summary: Davivienda reconoció fallas e intermitencias en sus canales virtuales este jueves, mientras usuarios reportan problemas para realizar distintas operaciones.
items.body: Davivienda reportó este jueves fallas e intermitencias en su aplicación móvil y página web, que afectan a clientes en Colombia. Los usuarios señalaron problemas para ingresar a sus cuentas, consultar saldos, realizar transferencias y efectuar pagos. “En el momento presentamos novedades e intermitencias en nuestros canales virtuales”, respondió el banco a través de sus canales de atención. Davivienda agregó que su equipo de tecnología trabaja para solucionar el inconveniente. Entre las operaciones que los clientes reportaron con problemas están las consultas de saldo, los envíos a Daviplata, las transferencias mediante Bre-B y los pagos a través de PSE. Davivienda tiene una participación relevante en Bre-B, el sistema del Banco de la República que permite realizar transferencias inmediatas entre entidades financieras mediante una llave. Según su presidente, Javier Suárez, el banco concentró 22% de las transacciones de Bre-B en 2025. La cuenta oficial de Davivienda en X respondió a los reclamos de usuarios y pidió a los afectados comunicarse mediante mensaje directo para revisar cada caso. No es la primera interrupción que afecta los canales digitales de Davivienda. El 14 de marzo de 2026, usuarios reportaron problemas con la aplicación y algunos cajeros automáticos. En octubre de 2025, el banco atribuyó otra interrupción a una caída global de Amazon Web Services (AWS), que afectó sus servicios y su línea telefónica. La falla de este jueves ocurre diez días antes de la integración de Davibank con Davivienda. Desde el 1 de noviembre, las operaciones de Davibank en Colombia pasarán a Davivienda, con el traslado de 3,5 millones de clientes y activos por cerca de $30 billones, según Suárez.

items.title: Un sismo de magnitud 7,0 sacude la región del Tíbet, en China
items.author: Brian K. Sullivan
items.summary: El sismo ocurrió al este-noreste de Nagqu, en la región del Tíbet, y fue seguido por una réplica de magnitud 5,2.
items.body: Bloomberg — Un fuerte terremoto sacudió la meseta tibetana en China el jueves. Un sismo de magnitud 7,0 se produjo a unos 191 kilómetros (119 millas) al este-noreste de Nagqu, en el Tíbet, alrededor de las 22:33 hora local, según el Servicio Geológico de los Estados Unidos (USGS). Le siguió una réplica de magnitud 5,2. La meseta tibetana ha sufrido varios terremotos importantes desde 1900. El USGS contabiliza 29 terremotos de magnitud superior a 7,0 “dentro de la meseta tibetana y a lo largo de las regiones colindantes” durante ese período. El sismo más potente, ocurrido en 1950, fue de magnitud 8,6 y causó la muerte de más de 4,000 personas, según informó. La agencia estatal de noticias Xinhua informó que el Ministerio de Gestión de Emergencias activó una respuesta de emergencia nacional de Nivel IV y envió un grupo de trabajo a la región afectada. La zona poco poblada alrededor del epicentro tiene una altitud promedio de unos 4,800 metros (15,750 pies). Hasta el momento no se han reportado víctimas ni daños. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Presidente da Romênia pede segurança a crianças após dois ataques violentos a escolas
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O presidente romeno, Nicusor Dan, pediu ao governo nesta quinta-feira que garanta a segurança das crianças nas salas de aula e na internet, após dois ataques violentos em escolas em menos de uma semana.
items.body:
O presidente romeno, Nicusor Dan, pediu ao governo nesta quinta-feira que garanta a segurança das crianças nas salas de aula e na internet, após dois ataques violentos em escolas em menos de uma semana.
A polícia informou que um adolescente de 15 anos atacou dois colegas de classe com um facão nesta quinta-feira em um banheiro de sua escola de ensino médio na cidade de Pitesti, na região central da Romênia.
Na segunda-feira, um estudante de 13 anos esfaqueou e feriu um professor e outro aluno. A mídia local informou que ele havia feito publicações sobre seus planos nas redes sociais pouco antes do ataque.
“Dois sinais que não podemos mais nos dar ao luxo de ignorar”, disse Dan em uma postagem no X.
“Precisamos de escolas mais seguras, professores apoiados e preparados para intervir, acesso real a aconselhamento psicológico, mas também medidas para a proteção de menores no uso do espaço online”, acrescentou o presidente centrista.
O governo recém-empossado da Romênia realizará uma reunião na sexta-feira para discutir medidas de segurança nas escolas.
As escolas na Europa enfrentaram uma série de ataques neste ano em países como Polônia, França e Suécia, com as autoridades, em alguns casos, apontando o papel das redes sociais e das subculturas online que glorificam o assassinato como fator que fomenta a violência.

Oct 22 : US President Donald Trump criticized NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behavior during the singing of the national anthem at a recent NBA game.
"While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country," Trump said in a Truth Social post accompanied by a video showing James moving his body during the singing of the anthem. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!"
The clip Trump shared showed James standing in line with the members of the Philadelphia 76ers, swinging his arms in a warmup-type stretch and performing basketball shooting movements.
A representative for the 76ers did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump has repeatedly criticized athletes for their behavior during pre-game renditions of the US national anthem, notably beginning with NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick's kneeling protest in support of racial justice.
Trump canceled a planned White House visit of the Super Bowl champions Philadelphia Eagles in 2018 after the team disagreed with his call for players to stand during the anthem.
James became a leading voice in the Black Lives Matter movement in 2020 and has frequently supported progressive issues as he ascended to the top of the NBA's all-time scoring list.

items.title: É falso que Flávio Bolsonaro tenha dito que férias de 30 dias são "exagero"
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: O candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) não afirmou que férias de 30 dias são "um exagero", como dizem publicações nas redes sociais.
items.body:
O candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) não afirmou que férias de 30 dias são "um exagero", como dizem publicações nas redes sociais.
Estes são os principais detalhes:
“Flávio: 'Trinta dias de férias é um exagero. Quinze dias é mais do que o suficiente'”, alegam os posts, que circulam no Facebook e no Instagram com uma foto do candidato.
A imagem tem o logotipo da Jovem Pan News, mas não há registro da suposta notícia nos perfis da emissora no Instagram , no Facebook e no X .
Além disso, a fonte usada nos posts é diferente da utilizada pela Jovem Pan News.
O plano de governo de Flávio apresentado ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) não menciona diminuir férias.
“O custo de um trabalhador formal chega a cerca de duas vezes o salário que ele leva para casa... Vamos reduzir gradualmente o custo do trabalho, sem retirar direitos”, diz o documento.
A Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT) assegura 30 dias de férias, sem prejuízo à remuneração, a cada ano de vigência do contrato de trabalho.
A assessoria do candidato não havia respondido a um pedido de comentário até a publicação deste texto.
Veredicto: Falso. Flávio Bolsonaro não disse que 30 dias de férias são um “exagero”, e a Jovem Pan News não publicou uma notícia com esta afirmação.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: Macron endurece restrições a protestos na França e culpa extrema-esquerda pelos distúrbios
items.author: Michel Rose
items.creator: Michel Rose
items.summary: O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que protestos “ilegítimos” seriam proibidos nos próximos dias e atribuiu a culpa aos grupos de extrema-esquerda “sediciosos” e aos vândalos pelos distúrbios e saques ocorridos no último fim de semana.
items.body:
O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que protestos “ilegítimos” seriam proibidos nos próximos dias e atribuiu a culpa aos grupos de extrema-esquerda “sediciosos” e aos vândalos pelos distúrbios e saques ocorridos no último fim de semana.
Após uma reunião com chefes de inteligência e ministros de alto escalão, Macron afirmou que manifestações organizadas por grupos como sindicatos teriam permissão para ocorrer, mas poderiam ser redirecionadas por percursos alternativos para proteger as lojas.
“No último sábado, tivemos atos políticos e sediciosos por parte de grupos de extrema-esquerda cujo objetivo é derrubar a República”, disse ele.
Seus comentários foram feitos enquanto as autoridades em toda a França se preparavam para novos protestos, após alguns dos piores distúrbios urbanos do país nos últimos anos.
O ministro da Justiça, Gérald Darmanin, disse que deseja a suspensão do direito de voto para pessoas que desrespeitem as proibições de participação em manifestações, bem como restrições ao acesso às redes sociais para pessoas envolvidas em violência, saques ou ataques à polícia.
Todos os protestos planejados para sábado em Marselha e Lyon, a segunda e a terceira maiores cidades da França, foram proibidos, informaram as autoridades locais. No entanto, novas manifestações já estão se organizando antes do que as autoridades temem que possa ser mais um fim de semana conturbado.
A principal união estudantil da França, a Unef, convocou manifestações para sábado, enquanto o movimento dos Coletes Amarelos, força antissistema que surgiu em 2018, apresentou planos para uma marcha pelo centro de Paris.
Comerciantes no centro de Paris começaram a proteger as vitrines de suas lojas com tábuas, em caso de violência. O grupo de artigos de luxo Hermès informou que reforçou as medidas de segurança em suas lojas na França.
Os organizadores da feira internacional de colecionadores de arte Art Basel Paris, realizada em um centro de exposições no centro de Paris, informaram que o evento ficará fechado durante todo o fim de semana.
Em outro local, as autoridades da cidade de Orléans, no norte do país, se preparavam para possíveis distúrbios, já que a extrema-direita, representada pelo Reunião Nacional, realizaria uma reunião anual, enquanto sindicatos e grupos de esquerda planejavam manifestações.
Um protesto estudantil convocado para quinta-feira em Paris foi inicialmente proibido, mas acabou sendo autorizado a ocorrer; no entanto, as estações de metrô no centro de Paris foram fechadas pelas autoridades de transporte público em antecipação a aglomerações não autorizadas.
INDIGNAÇÃO PÚBLICA A França foi abalada em 17 de outubro por atos de violência à margem dos protestos em todo o país, expondo a profundidade da indignação pública e levantando dúvidas sobre a capacidade dos serviços de segurança de manter a ordem.
Duas pessoas foram presas por um incêndio criminoso na prefeitura de Limoges, segundo autoridades francesas e a mídia.
A terceira noite consecutiva de toques de recolher locais transcorreu sem incidentes graves nas áreas afetadas pela violência, proporcionando ao governo um certo alívio antes do fim de semana.
A agitação revelou um mal-estar mais profundo na França, onde os custos crescentes da energia, a pressão sobre o orçamento familiar e as preocupações com a deterioração dos serviços públicos têm alimentado uma frustração crescente entre os trabalhadores e os jovens.
A classe política francesa também mergulhou em uma acirrada troca de acusações, com o governo acusando grupos políticos de extrema-esquerda de alimentar a agitação.
Destacando o mal-estar dos investidores, o prêmio de risco da dívida pública francesa em relação aos títulos alemães, considerados refúgios seguros, ampliou-se nesta quinta-feira para o maior nível em 15 anos, enquanto o rendimento do título de referência francês de 10 anos atingiu 5,14%, seu nível mais alto desde julho de 2002.

items.title: Canadian dollar extends daily winning streak as interest rate spreads narrow
items.author: Fergal Smith
items.creator: Fergal Smith
items.summary: The Canadian dollar strengthened to a one-month high against its US counterpart on Thursday as oil prices rose and the gap narrowed between US and Canadian interest rates.
items.body:
The Canadian dollar strengthened to a one-month high against its US counterpart on Thursday as oil prices rose and the gap narrowed between US and Canadian interest rates.
The loonie was trading 0.3% higher at 1.4007 per US dollar, or 71.39 US cents, its strongest intraday level since September 21 and putting the currency on course for the sixth straight day of gains. The daily winning streak would be the longest since April.
"Most importantly for the currency, the repricing of the Bank of Canada outlook has narrowed the two-year US-Canada yield spread," said Kevin Ford, an FX & macro strategist at Convera. "That has reduced the US dollar’s rate advantage at the same time that elevated oil prices have supported Canada’s terms of trade."
The gap between Canada's 2-year yield and the equivalent US rate narrowed by 11 basis points to about 141 basis points in favor of the US note.
Concerns about the sustainability of the AI outlook resurfaced, boosting the [USN:L6N468126 TEXT:"safe-haven appeal"] of US Treasuries.
The price of [USN:L1N46801N TEXT:"oil"], one of Canada's major exports, rose after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns of further disruption to energy supplies from the key exporting region. US crude oil futures were trading 2.2% higher at $99.26 a barrel.
"The USD-CAD is looking to test the 1.40 level on the downside, but extending the move below that threshold will likely require further support from Canadian data and the Bank of Canada," Ford said.
Investors see a roughly 75% chance the Bank of Canada will raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% next Wednesday. Bets on a hike have increased in recent days after hawkish comments from BoC Governor Tiff Macklem and evidence of rising expectations for long-term inflation.
Canadian retail sales data for August is due on Friday — analysts expect sales to rebound 1.3% after they declined 0.7% in July.
Canadian government bonds tracked the moves in US Treasuries. The 10-year yield was down 7.8 basis points at 3.787%.

items.title: New Zealand Cost Crisis Drives Election Vows to Rein In Business
items.author: Tracy Withers
items.creator: Tracy Withers
items.summary: In New Zealand, the rising price of everyday items is sobering: bread costs 64% more than three years ago, butter is up 57% and electricity 27%. Hikes like these are causing politicians across the spectrum to propose radical market interventions to improve competition and lower costs ahead of next month’s election.

items.title: Estado de Rhode Island processa Meta por suposta tolerância a anúncios fraudulentos
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O estado de Rhode Island, nos Estados Unidos, processou a Meta nesta quinta-feira em um tribunal estadual, devido à suposta tolerância da empresa à publicidade fraudulenta generalizada em suas plataformas Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp.
items.body:
O estado de Rhode Island, nos Estados Unidos, processou a Meta (META.O) nesta quinta-feira em um tribunal estadual, devido à suposta tolerância da empresa à publicidade fraudulenta generalizada em suas plataformas Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp.
O processo, movido pelo Procurador-Geral de Rhode Island, Peter Neronha, no Tribunal Superior de Providence, acusa a Meta de lucrar ilegalmente e participar da criação de bilhões de dólares em publicidade fraudulenta – mesmo enquanto assegurava a seus bilhões de usuários que estava trabalhando diligentemente para protegê-los.
Este é o primeiro caso relacionado a golpes desse tipo movido contra a Meta por um estado dos EUA, após uma ação semelhante apresentada em maio pelo Condado de Santa Clara, na Califórnia.
O processo busca indenizações civis monetárias por cada uma das supostas violações da lei estadual de Rhode Island cometidas pela Meta, restituição aos consumidores, devolução dos lucros ilícitos e uma ordem judicial que obrigue a empresa a lidar com os anúncios fraudulentos que desenvolve e veicula em suas plataformas, em vez de lucrar com eles.
"Conforme alegado, Meta expôs conscientemente usuários vulneráveis a fraudes e golpes, obtendo lucros enormes com isso. Quando empresas, grandes ou pequenas, se aproveitam dos consumidores de Rhode Island, este escritório fará tudo ao seu alcance para responsabilizá-las", disse Neronha em um comunicado à imprensa.
O processo cita reportagem da Reuters do ano passado sobre documentos internos da meta que detalham a vasta escala de publicidade fraudulenta nas plataformas da empresa – e os cálculos da Meta de que estava lucrando muito mais com anúncios fraudulentos de alto risco do que esperava pagar em multas por permiti-los.
De acordo com esses documentos, a Meta exibe cerca de 15 bilhões de anúncios fraudulentos de "alto risco" para os usuários todos os dias e obteve aproximadamente 10% de sua receita de 2024 com comércio eletrônico fraudulento, produtos de saúde duvidosos e outros tipos de marketing proibidos.
Em muitos casos, a ação judicial de Rhode Island alegou que as ferramentas de criação de anúncios com IA da Meta ajudaram ativamente os golpistas em suas práticas de marketing fraudulentas. Em vez de bloquear consistentemente os anunciantes que seus sistemas automatizados de detecção suspeitavam de fraude, Rhode Island alegou que a meta às vezes cobrava deles um valor extra como penalidade.
"A Meta ajudou conscientemente a criar e otimizar esses anúncios para garantir que fossem o mais eficazes possível e, em seguida, mentiu sobre eles, deturpando para o público seu compromisso de prevenir fraudes em suas plataformas", afirmou o processo.
A Meta não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário sobre o caso. A empresa contestou a reportagem da Reuters.
"Combatemos agressivamente fraudes e golpes porque as pessoas em nossas plataformas não querem esse tipo de conteúdo, os anunciantes legítimos não o querem e nós também não", disse Andy Stone, porta-voz da Meta, em resposta à reportagem do ano passado, classificando-a como "uma visão seletiva que distorce a abordagem da Meta em relação a fraudes e golpes".
Nos meses que se seguiram à publicação das reportagens da Reuters, a Meta alegou ter feito progressos em suas iniciativas de combate a golpes. No entanto, Rhode Island afirmou que os golpes continuam desenfreados e facilmente encontrados na biblioteca de anúncios da empresa, um banco de dados de anúncios veiculados nas plataformas da Meta.
"O anúncio abaixo, por exemplo, prometia reverter Alzheimer em 45 dias", afirmou a denúncia de Rhode Island sobre um conjunto de anúncios fraudulentos. "Havia mais de 2.000 versões desse anúncio ativas na biblioteca de Meta Ads."
COM FOCO NO PÚBLICO IDOSO Segundo apurou o estado de Rhode Island, os anúncios fraudulentos frequentemente tinham como alvo pessoas idosas, citando uma investigação do Centro para o Combate ao Ódio Digital (Center for Countering Digital Hate), uma organização sem fins lucrativos que identificou quase 94.000 anúncios fraudulentos nas plataformas da Meta.
"Alguns desses anunciantes gastaram mais em anúncios da Meta ao longo de vários anos do que grandes marcas como Walmart ou Pfizer", afirmou o processo.
Além dos golpes, o gabinete do procurador-geral de Rhode Island afirmou ter constatado que a Meta também estava falhando em fiscalizar outros tipos de anúncios ilícitos, como os de aplicativos de IA para pornografia deepfake. Em um exemplo fornecido pelo estado, um anúncio mostrava imagens lado a lado de uma mulher totalmente vestida em uma cafeteria, ao lado de uma imagem dela praticando um ato sexual.
Rhode Island também citou exemplos de anúncios fraudulentos que se fazem passar por figuras públicas e instituições confiáveis, como bancos, para tirar proveito de sua credibilidade, incluindo um caso em que golpistas na China usaram o nome e a imagem de um alto executivo do Bank of America em anúncios no Facebook e Instagram que atraíam usuários para negociações fraudulentas de ações no WhatsApp.
Dados de pesquisas públicas citados por Rhode Island – e avaliações internas da Meta obtidas pela Reuters – indicam que as plataformas da empresa são responsáveis por uma parcela desproporcional de golpes online e que as defesas da meta contra golpes eram mais fracas do que as de seus principais concorrentes em publicidade digital.
"É mais fácil anunciar golpes em plataformas Meta do que no Google", concluiu uma análise interna da Meta em abril de 2025.
Apesar disso, a Meta tentou frustrar os esforços regulatórios para exigir verificação, afirmou Rhode Island.
O processo alegava que "um anunciante banido pode reaparecer no tempo necessário para fornecer um novo endereço de email ou número de telefone".
(Por Jeff Horwitz e Katie Paul)

items.title: ECB's Santos Pereira pushes for deeper EU integration
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: ECB policymaker Alvaro Santos Pereira said on Thursday that Europe's difficult geopolitical environment and technological shortcomings show it is time to give fresh momentum to European integration by deepening the single market in services, transport and energy.
items.body:
ECB policymaker Alvaro Santos Pereira said on Thursday that Europe's difficult geopolitical environment and technological shortcomings show it is time to give fresh momentum to European integration by deepening the single market in services, transport and energy.
The remarks by Portugal's central bank governor add to growing calls from European policymakers to deepen integration and remove barriers seen as weighing on the bloc's competitiveness and growth.
The single market reduced many forms of fragmentation, he noted, but significant barriers persist.
The remaining challenges are more complex because they are rooted in national institutions and regulations, he said at a conference.
It was vital to complete integration in areas where it remains limited, including services, transport and energy, he added.

items.title: Paraguay's central bank under pressure over politically connected lender
items.author: Daniela Desantis
items.creator: Daniela Desantis
items.summary: Paraguay's central bank and its president face mounting calls to resign as scrutiny intensifies over how they supervised a fast-growing digital bank with political ties.
items.body:
Paraguay's central bank and its president face mounting calls to resign as scrutiny intensifies over how they supervised a fast-growing digital bank with political ties.
Senators from the ruling party and the opposition have urged President Santiago Peña to remove the central bank's top leadership, despite it being credited with helping [USN:S0N3ZU04S TEXT:"Paraguay"] secure investment-grade status.
The case is testing the reputation that has helped Paraguay become one of South America's emerging destinations for foreign capital, much of it from neighboring Brazil.
In recent weeks, authorities have repeatedly tried to calm financial markets after it emerged that ueno bank faced regulatory scrutiny of its business and an administrative investigation. The bank uses lower case in company statements.
In written statements to Reuters, Paraguay's central bank defended its governance structure, saying regulatory and supervisory processes operate independently and in accordance with established legal procedures.
Ueno said it would continue to "fully cooperate" with the central bank and maintained that the preliminary administrative proceeding did not constitute a finding of wrongdoing.
Ueno has scaled rapidly from a niche local fintech player to a mid-tier bank, in line with digital platforms like [USN:L6N45I01U TEXT:"Monzo"] and [USN:S0N44O08P TEXT:"Nubank"]. It says it has 3 million customers and manages roughly $800 million to $850 million in public funds.
Details of the preliminary probe appeared in a central bank report sent to the Senate this month. The report aimed to dispel doubts about loans issued by ueno to related companies, but it ended up fueling more questions from lawmakers, the banking association and other business groups.
"The replacement of the Central Bank authorities must take place," ruling-party Senator Gustavo Leite said in an interview with Reuters. "The people at the Central Bank have lost credibility."
Opposition Senator Rafael Filizzola said the financial system was "suffering" and filed another request for information on ueno, which experienced a major selloff of its global bonds. Fitch Ratings changed the outlook on the company's securities from stable to negative last week.
Paraguay's Banking Association, which represents 14 private lenders including Brazil's Itau [RIC:RIC:ITUPU.UL], published a statement on October 18 reiterating that the central bank's response to the senate was "incomplete."
POLITICAL TIES The case is politically sensitive. Paraguay's central bank president, Carlos Carvallo, previously worked at ueno and served as its president until August 2023, the company confirmed in a statement to Reuters. Peña, a former [USN:L4N3K813R TEXT:"economist"], was a business partner of the group that owned the bank until March 2025. Ueno said Peña never had a relationship with the bank itself as a shareholder or investor.
Much of the pressure for answers has come from lawmakers of the ruling Colorado Party, amid an internal dispute over the party's presidential nomination for the 2028 general elections.
In a written response to Reuters, the central bank said there was no conflict of interest, saying Carvallo had "recused himself" from all decisions related to ueno bank.
Paraguay’s presidency did not respond to a request for comment.
In remarks to local media in early October, Peña described the situation as an "overflow" of a technical matter that was taken into the political arena and had done "tremendous damage to the image of the entire country."
The ueno case has put a spotlight on stability in Paraguay's grain-exporting economy that won investment-grade credit ratings from Moody's in 2024 and S&P Global last year.
The IMF expects growth of 4.5% this year, almost double the [USN:L6N46117N TEXT:"regional average"].

items.title: Zelenski afirma que aún no se ha restablecido velocidad de Starlink, espera hablar con Marco Rubio
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El presidente Volodimir Zelenski afirmó el jueves que aún no se ha restablecido la velocidad de Starlink en Ucrania, y añadió que espera mantener conversaciones con el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, en los próximos días.
items.body:
El presidente Volodimir Zelenski afirmó el jueves que aún no se ha restablecido la velocidad de Starlink en Ucrania, y añadió que espera mantener conversaciones con el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, en los próximos días.
Zelenski señaló que Ucrania está dispuesta a participar en conversaciones de paz durante la cumbre del G20 en Estados Unidos, pero que, hasta el momento, no se había recibido ninguna invitación al respecto.
"Hay claramente una cuestión en juego: obligar a Rusia a poner fin a esta guerra", dijo el mandatario a periodistas en Kiev.
"Es posible (...) con la mediación del presidente (Donald) Trump y de nuestros socios. Creo que todo es posible, y podemos contar con una reunión en Florida durante la cumbre del G20", agregó.

items.title: Why Anthropic is turning away some users
items.author: Krystal Hu
items.creator: Krystal Hu
items.summary: Bill Gross, founder of Idealab, is Silicon Valley’s idea guy.
items.body:
Bill Gross, founder of Idealab, is Silicon Valley’s idea guy.
Over 30 years, he’s developed a methodology for spotting business ideas and used it to help start 175 companies through his incubator, with more than 45 exits.
So it stung a little when, a few months ago, Gross found that AI had gotten disturbingly good at generating business ideas. He told me it left him feeling “depressed”. Then the feeling turned into an idea itself: what if he turned his methodology into a system anyone could use?
That system, Idealab.ai , launched this week. It matches your background and skills against AI-generated business ideas, and lets you set the budget you’re willing to work with.
Not every idea it spits out is going to be a great business, but Gross is betting the platform can lower the barrier to entrepreneurship for people who’d never otherwise know where to start.
The human part, he insists, doesn’t go away. “All the judgment and decisions still have to be made by humans,” he told me. AI can offer suggestions, “but you have to make the call.” And, “you’ve got to be passionate about it, for sure.”
OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L4N4661IU TEXT:"Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger is 'a good idea' as companies form deal committees"]
[USN:FWN4661WE TEXT:"Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centers popular"]
[USN:L6N46701V TEXT:"OpenAI says its AI agents weakened internal monitoring system"]
[USN:L4N4660IQ TEXT:"Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows"]
[USN:L6N4661EP TEXT:"SpaceX and Tesla's Terafab targets 2028 for volume chip production, Musk says"]
[USN:L8N4650GT TEXT:"ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent place over $35 billion worth of Nvidia chip orders"]
ANTHROPIC'S FIGHT WITH DISTILLATION Here’s a strange move for a company racing toward the largest IPO in history: turn away paying customers, on purpose, weeks before you go public. That’s effectively what Anthropic just did.
Inside an investor meeting in San Francisco last week, my colleagues and I got a [USN:L6N4601AA TEXT:"behind-the-scenes look"] at how Anthropic’s executives are explaining a slowdown of their own making.
The company has cut off a meaningful slice of paying customers — accounting for between 5% and 7% of its revenue in the first nine months of the year, investors at the meeting told us. The reasoning: those accounts weren’t typical customers. They were, Anthropic alleged, Chinese AI labs quietly mining Claude to train their own models.
The technique is known as distillation in AI model development. A smaller “student” model learns by studying the outputs of a larger “teacher” model, essentially absorbing its capabilities secondhand. In February, [USN:L4N3ZJ1G1 TEXT:"Anthropic said"] Chinese labs including DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax had generated more than 16 million interactions with Claude through roughly 24,000 fake accounts, all in violation of its terms of service.
Anthropic calls this more than a contract violation. It considers the practice a loss of intellectual property with national security implications. So the company rolled out new defenses earlier this month: applying access restrictions, proxy blocking, and bans on tens of thousands of accounts, which it says has cut off 90% to 99% of the data being siphoned.
Anthropic is telling investors the crackdown has effectively stopped Chinese developers from distilling its models.
Here’s why that matters for the IPO: it gives Anthropic a tidy explanation for something investors were already nervous about — a month-to-month growth deceleration. It may also address a bigger worry. Anthropic is betting that cutting off Chinese labs will slow their progress, not just stop a few bad actors from gaming the terms of service.
The underlying numbers are still extraordinary by any standard. By this past March, Anthropic had already brought in $4.7 billion in a single quarter — more than all of 2025. Then it kept climbing: $11.6 billion in the second quarter, $16.8 billion in the third.
But growth at that scale doesn’t usually keep compounding at the same rate forever. Competition from cheaper, open-source Chinese models remains one of the most common concerns investors are raising.
Reuters has reported that [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"some investors are now discussing"] a valuation near $1.5 trillion for the IPO, down from the roughly $2 trillion once expected. The real question is whether this crackdown — and the short-term revenue hit that comes with it — actually buys Anthropic a lasting distance from its open-source rivals, or just a temporary edge.
CHART OF THE WEEK According to [USN:L6N4650MN TEXT:"a new survey"] of more than 380 security and technology professionals by Salt Security, 86% of their organizations now have at least one AI agent operating, and 77% have agents chaining actions together across other agents. In other words, agents aren’t just answering questions anymore — they’re taking multi-step actions, often autonomously, deep inside company systems.
What’s missing is the ability to actually watch them. Only 18% of those same organizations say they can automatically stop an agent that starts behaving unexpectedly, and just 13% can trace a complete path from instruction to outcome across every agent involved. That’s a massive visibility gap between how fast companies are deploying agents and how well they can monitor what those agents are actually doing.

items.title: The midterms reach Kyiv
items.author: Trevor Hunnicutt
items.creator: Trevor Hunnicutt
items.summary: US President Donald Trump has not so quietly shifted course on a major policy issue in the past month. After criticizing Russian President Vladimir Putin, he's started to make nice. What explains the turnabout? The November midterms may offer a clue.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump has not so quietly shifted course on a major policy issue in the past month. After criticizing Russian President Vladimir Putin, he's started to make nice. What explains the turnabout? The November midterms may offer a clue.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, once Washington's most celebrated wartime ally, is finding himself caught in the crossfire of US midterm politics. He is under mounting pressure from Trump to strike a peace deal with Putin.
With US voters increasingly frustrated by[USN:L6N45Z19G TEXT:" high energy prices"] and the cost of living, Trump has turned renewed attention to the war in Ukraine in recent days, arguing that a negotiated settlement there could help ease economic pressures at home, even though US consumers would be unlikely to feel the effects of any peace deal ahead of the November 3 vote.
Trump has said the war may be closer than ever to finishing and that he wants the death and destruction to end. But he also may be betting that a resolution of the four-year conflict could ease pressures on the US economy, voters’ pocketbooks and his own political fortunes. Russia is a major oil supplier and has held out the possibility of a broad economic pact with Washington.
In recent weeks, Trump has cut a deal with Putin, temporarily easing US sanctions on Russian diesel (and [USN:FWN4622VQ TEXT:"waiving others"]) in exchange for Moscow providing more diesel to global markets. He’s considering a [USN:SPN45Y0Z6 TEXT:"meeting with Putin"] and Chinese President Xi Jinping next month, without Zelenskiy. Meanwhile, Kyiv has [USN:P8N41Y023 TEXT:"complained that a satellite system"] made by US-based SpaceX has stopped working when mounted on fast-moving drones, limiting its ability to strike Russian targets and defend against attacks.
The moves are a shift from Trump’s earlier [USN:S0N3S902L TEXT:"criticisms of Putin"] and a return to [USN:L2N3PI1I7 TEXT:"more prickly relations"] between the US and Ukrainian leaders. Ukraine and several European allies have expressed alarm at an apparent pivot by Trump.
Trump has blamed [USN:L8N4620HY TEXT:"Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries"] for driving up global diesel prices. He’s also suggested that Ukraine needs a new leader. “Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine,” he told us at the White House on Monday. “Zelenskiy is not helping matters much.” Trump envoy Steve Witkoff later called Putin a “humanitarian” for [USN:L8N4670ON TEXT:"freeing a retired US schoolteacher"] in custody since 2022.
The Ukrainian attacks have contributed to higher diesel prices, although market analysts attribute most of the increase to disruptions in fuel shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. That’s a consequence of a different war: the US-led one with Iran.
Trump wouldn’t be the first politician to lay blame for inflation abroad. His Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, [USN:L2N2VC04A TEXT:"pointed to Putin"] after Russia's invasion of Ukraine caused gasoline prices to surge ahead of congressional elections in 2022.
Voters are not buying a similar argument from Trump. Some 78% of Americans say his policies bear at least some blame for rising prices, according to a [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"]. Most Republicans and Democrats cited the cost of living as their top concern.
Zelenskiy told visiting US lawmakers on Monday that recent “decisions on the American side … are [USN:L4N4651HF TEXT:"hard to explain"].”
For the answer, he may need to look no further than the US political calendar.

POLL OF THE WEEK Your questions on election officials’ preparations for violent or legal threats How are election officials preparing for threats to poll workers, misinformation, administrative disruptions or attempts to interfere with voting and vote counting?
Reuters interviewed more than 50 state and local election officials from both political parties, including a dozen secretaries of state, the top election officials in their states. Nearly all said they are adopting new strategies to prepare for political interference, misinformation, cyberattacks and even threats of violence ahead of the midterms. Their efforts span jurisdictions large and small, in areas controlled by Trump’s Republican Party as well as the opposition Democratic Party. In Michigan, for example, state officials are advising local clerks on the appropriate response if the federal government demands access to voting machines.
Preparations fall into three categories. Some election officials are hiring lawyers or seeking legal skills, as over a dozen interviewees said. Twice that many election officials said they are expanding public outreach and social media campaigns to counter misinformation around the reliability of mail-in voting or voting machines. Most of the interviewed officials said they are scrambling to fill gaps left by the Trump administration’s cuts to programs that help safeguard elections from cyberattacks and physical security threats. That includes ongoing work to fortify election offices with camera systems and bulletproof glass – a trend that began after Trump disputed his loss to Biden in the 2020 election, prompting violent threats by Trump supporters against election workers .
Read our reporting on more specific examples of what election officials are doing in preparation for such potential scenarios in Wisconsin, North Carolina, Georgia, Michigan, Colorado, and Maine.
THE VIEW FROM PARIS The French government is bracing for the prospect of more protests as soon as this weekend after some of the [USN:L8N46401O TEXT:"worst urban tumult"] in years. Thousands were arrested, and shops looted, amid nationwide protests on October 17 over high prices and declining public services. Trump has weighed in repeatedly on the crisis, blaming immigrants and radical Islam for the violence, without providing evidence. In Kansas on Monday, Trump warned voters that the US would [USN:L1N4650ZT TEXT:"burn like France"] if Democrats win. Macron [USN:L8N4670KY TEXT:"shot back"] that Trump and other foreign leaders had spread misinformation about what happened and were looking to score political points at France's expense. He called comments by foreign leaders "stupid" and "unacceptable."

items.title: US blocks two devices with Chinese-made surveillance chips
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it had blocked two devices from the US market that contain foreign surveillance chips produced by a subsidiary of China's Huawei, the first time it had exercised authority under new rules.
items.body:
The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it had blocked two devices from the US market that contain foreign surveillance chips produced by a subsidiary of China's Huawei, the first time it had exercised authority under new rules.
The US telecom agency said it barred a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter containing chips produced by Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon, which the agency said advertises its chip as "designed for the surveillance market" and including "detection algorithms for human faces."
FCC Chair Brendan Carr said video devices containing surveillance chips produced by companies on its national security list "pose an obvious and unacceptable risk to the nation and our people."
Huawei did not immediately respond to a request for comment and HiSilicon could not immediately be reached.
The FCC voted in July to bar sales of devices in the US that contain key hardware from Chinese companies deemed to be national security risks
The Trump administration has mounted a sweeping crackdown on Chinese technology gear

items.title: Romania to speed up development of Black Sea capabilities after cargo ship attacks
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Romania will accelerate its development of surveillance capabilities and equipment to counter mines and drones in the Black Sea after a series of drone attacks on commercial ships off its coast, its top defence council said on Thursday.
items.body:
Romania will accelerate its development of surveillance capabilities and equipment to counter mines and drones in the Black Sea after a series of drone attacks on commercial ships off its coast, its top defence council said on Thursday.
At least [USN:L8N4610EC TEXT:"seven cargo ships"] have been hit near the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria in the past two weeks, with some 30 sailors reported dead or missing. Romanian F-16 fighter jet pilots [USN:L1N46306E TEXT:"shot down"] two of the latest generation of Russian drones over Romanian territorial waters on Saturday.
[USN:L6N46613E TEXT:"NATO"] said on Tuesday it will send more maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems and drones to the Black Sea.
Romania's top defence council said latest ship attacks are direct consequences of Russia's aggression beyond Ukraine's borders.
Threats to freedom of navigation and critical energy projects in the Black Sea pose a security crisis for Romania.
The current risks require concrete measures to protect human lives, maintain free access to national ports, and ensure the security of energy facilities in the Exclusive Economic Zone.
The top defence council said it will accelerate the development of capabilities for maritime surveillance, countering naval mines and intervening against drones illegally breaching national airspace and waters.
Authorities will practice to improve the efficiency of their operational response.
Romania will seek to improve cooperation with fellow NATO members [USN:L8N43A0JZ TEXT:"Bulgaria and Turkey"] with whom it shares the Black Sea.
"The Council members also analyzed ways to intensify coordination within NATO. This includes strengthening the deterrence and defense posture on the Eastern Flank and identifying new measures to respond to threats in the Black Sea region."

items.title: Nigeria says Ebola case remains isolated, urges calm
items.author: Camillus Eboh
items.creator: Camillus Eboh
items.summary: Nigeria's health minister said on Thursday authorities had no evidence that the country's recently confirmed Ebola case had spread into the wider community, describing it as a single, contained infection.
items.body:
Nigeria's health minister said on Thursday authorities had no evidence that the country's recently [USN:L6N4670RQ TEXT:"confirmed Ebola case"] had spread into the wider community, describing it as a single, contained infection.
Nigeria reported its first Ebola case in more than a decade on Tuesday, becoming the fourth African country and the most populous yet to be affected by an outbreak that health officials have described as the [USN:L6N4421DF TEXT:"fastest-spreading on record"].
Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said "there is no evidence that it has gone into the communities" and that there was "no need for any panic", as health officials intensified contact tracing and monitoring of people who may have been exposed
"This is a contained, single case and we are diligently working to ensure that it remains so," he said
Pate said there was no reason at present to alter plans for large public gatherings, but left open the possibility of additional measures if the situation worsened
"We have only one case, and hopefully it will stay that way," he said
